source.title: Feature-Learning Networks Are Consistent Across Widths At Realistic Scales
source.authors: Nikhil Vyas; Alexander Atanasov; Blake Bordelon; Depen Morwani; Sabarish Sainathan; Cengiz Pehlevan

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own width-sweep training results, including near-zero training error in offline settings that fails to converge across widths, qualifying the claim's account of width and training time.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss/error and width comparisons that bear on V1 and V3's training-error claims. Its width-consistency results do not test the other versions. Values visible only in plots without stated numeric values are recorded as figure only. Cited prior work is not treated as this paper's result.
record.test_reason: Section 3.2 reports near-zero offline training error for convolutional networks on CIFAR-derived datasets, bearing on V1 in a new setting. Failure of errors to agree across widths does not establish failure to achieve near-zero error. No depth or shortcut comparison tests V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors find practical-width consistency in predictions, representations, losses, and dynamical phenomena under µP, with accumulating finite-width deviations at later times or after repeated data. Their conclusion concerns fixed training time and does not establish a joint infinite-width, infinite-training-time limit.
record.recipe_differences: Width sweep in µP with online or offline training and measurements of training loss/error; not a direct replication of the cited studies' recipes or claim interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with width, task complexity, online versus offline training, training duration, and label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Online loss curves agree across sufficiently large widths, while repeated data and later training amplify width-dependent differences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-learning networks in µP exhibit practical-width consistency whose accuracy depends on task, training duration, and data repetition.

fits_no_version.finding: Some narrower ensembles outperform wider ensembles on noisy-label test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider ensembles need not generalize better during offline training with label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 6 shows sharpness rising to a fluctuating plateau in large-batch SGD; Figures 6 and 15 show width-consistent large-learning-rate fluctuations in µP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-batch analogues of stability-related dynamics can be consistent across widths under µP.

record.code_released: The authors state: "We plan to have our code made freely available on github"; no URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2023, 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
record.problems: The paper's main width-consistency experiments measure crossentropy training loss rather than classification error. Training-error outcomes for offline settings are described qualitatively and shown in plots without exact values in text. The noisy-label condition is CIFAR-50k with 50% noisy labels, not CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Some figures show separate width curves without numerical values; the extraction records only outcomes stated in text and does not reconstruct values from plots.

untested.parts: Exact CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training-classification-error results; fully random labels; systematic effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization. The noisy-label endpoint cannot be determined from the supplied figure text.
Two-layer ReLU teacher–student spurious minima and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, matched identity-shortcut comparisons, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and maximum trainable depth.
Recovery above a measured initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction during recovery, full-batch tracking of the stability threshold, and divergence from initially subthreshold rates.
Matched comparisons of batch normalization versus no normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training speed or stability.

missing.what: Width-specific single-network training-error endpoints for noisy CIFAR-50k are needed to decide whether corrupted-label training reaches near-zero error. The current rows report width gaps instead.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted limits_scope verdicts. V3 is untested, and nonzero width-dependent bias or variance does not imply substantial training error. CIFAR-50k here is sampled from CIFAR-5m; it should not be identified with the standard CIFAR-10 training set.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 with random or corrupted labels as in the version's cited studies; the noisy-label experiment uses CIFAR-50k, 50% noisy labels, and reports training-error curves without exact values in text. CIFAR-5m is a distinct dataset.

Does not compare plain networks with and without identity shortcuts or test whether depth causes higher training error. Its offline-training and width comparisons only bear on whether near-zero training error and width consistency depend on setting.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across widths during online CIFAR-5m training.

conditions.value: one pass through 5 million image dataset

rows.value: Widths as narrow as 128 are essentially consistent with infinite width-behavior for an entire pass through the 5 million image dataset.
rows.note: The text describes online training-loss curves, not classification error. It gives no exact loss values.
rows.check: Width consistency of online crossentropy loss does not measure near-zero training classification error.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared training error across widths and with online training on CIFAR-200k.
rows.value: Offline single-network training error does not converge with width, even at high widths; both bias and variance for train error are magnified by offline training and do not tend to 0 for the largest widths tried.
rows.note: The paper says offline training achieves near-zero error, but the plotted errors and their width dependence are not numerically stated. Figure 8 reports values graphically.
rows.check: Section 3.2 explicitly describes offline training as achieving near-zero error. Nonzero bias and variance across widths do not contradict that statement. Remove V3; depth and shortcuts are not varied. The dataset is a CIFAR-5m subset, not CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2; Figure 8(a) and caption; Appendix A.2.1

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared training error for ensembled networks across widths on CIFAR-200k.
rows.value: Ensembling reveals that both bias and variance terms individually fail to reach zero, even at high widths.
rows.note: The result is stated qualitatively; exact values are only plotted.
rows.check: Ensemble performance and the width-dependent bias–variance decomposition do not establish the training error attained by an individual trained network. No depth intervention tests V3.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared single-network and ensemble training error across widths on noisy CIFAR-50k.
rows.value: The paper reports large bias and variance terms at large widths for multi-epoch training on noisy CIFAR-50k.
rows.note: The text gives no exact training-error values; the figure shows the curves.
rows.check: The noisy-label single-network training-error curves bear on V1, but large bias and variance across widths do not establish substantial absolute training error. The supplied figure text does not permit reliable width-specific endpoint readings. Separate single-network and ensemble results.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared training error across widths in offline and online CIFAR-200k training.
rows.value: Offline single-network performance on the training set does not converge with width, even at high widths.
rows.note: This duplicates the paper's separately shown offline-versus-online training-error comparison; the text does not give exact values.
rows.check: Duplicates R2 and should be removed. Width inconsistency is not evidence against near-zero training error.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Compared noisy CIFAR-50k training error across widths and ensemble status.
rows.value: Some ensembled narrower-width networks outperform ensembled wider networks; the plotted training-error curves show large bias and variance terms at large widths.
rows.note: The prose explicitly describes the large bias and variance; the figure supplies the width-specific curves without exact values.
rows.check: Duplicates the noisy-label comparison in R4. The narrower-ensemble advantage is a test-error result in Figure 8(f), not the training-error result in Figure 8(c).

rows.subject: ConvNeXt-T (tiny)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across widths during repeated ImageNet training.

conditions.value: beyond 40,000 training steps or five epochs

rows.baseline: early training, when loss curves are consistent across widths
rows.value: As networks overfit the training data, beyond 40,000 training steps or five epochs, the loss curves diverge dramatically for different-width networks; width consistency subsequently erodes.
rows.locator: Appendix I, Figure 19 and accompanying text
rows.note: The text describes loss-curve divergence, not classification training error; values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Correct the subject to ConvNeXt-T. Separation of crossentropy curves across widths tests width consistency, not near-zero classification error, depth degradation, or shortcut prevention.

relationships.condition: Offline ResNet18 training on CIFAR-200k, a subset of CIFAR-5m
relationships.reason: Section 3.2 explicitly reports near-zero offline training error (R2); remaining differences across widths do not negate near-zero error.
relationships.display_finding: Offline training error approached zero despite remaining differences across widths.

relation.reason: The study reports its own training-error results bearing directly on V1.

tranche.reason: Near-zero training error in a CIFAR-derived dataset under µP extends V1 to a new training setting.

source_check.notes: Width consistency and attainment of near-zero training error are distinct findings. The CIFAR models use µP and replace ResNet18 BatchNorm with LayerNorm; width-specific final errors are not numerically stated.

statements.correction: Offline ResNet18 training on CIFAR-200k, a random 200k-example subset of CIFAR-5m, achieves near-zero training error. Multi-epoch training is compared with online training across widths. Code release is planned in the introduction.
statements.problem: The training result and dataset description are correct. Released study code is not established by the supplied text, which only promises future availability.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Training loss is described as near width-consistent at widths as narrow as 128, while online classification error and random/corrupted labels are not measured (R1). Offline CIFAR-200k and noisy CIFAR-50k results indicate training error need not converge to zero across widths (R2–R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: offline multi-epoch CIFAR-200k, noisy CIFAR-50k, and ImageNet training
reader_labels.reason: Offline training results show width consistency eroding or training-error bias and variance failing to reach zero; the study does not test depth or identity shortcuts (R2–R7).
